entities.summary:
Complutense University of Madrid, founded in 1970, is a prominent public university located in Madrid, Spain, and is one of the oldest universities in the Spanish-speaking world, tracing its origins back to the 13th century. It is situated in Southern Europe and has played a crucial role in shaping the academic landscape of Spain and beyond, influencing numerous fields including humanities, sciences, and social studies.

The university has been home to notable figures such as philosopher José Ortega y Gasset and Nobel laureate Severo Ochoa, contributing to significant advancements in their respective fields. Its establishment marked a pivotal moment in the democratization of higher education in Spain, coinciding with the period of political transition following Franco's dictatorship. The Complutense's comprehensive curriculum and research initiatives have produced thousands of graduates who have gone on to influence various sectors across the globe.

The legacy of the Complutense University extends beyond its immediate educational impact; it has been instrumental in fostering a culture of critical thought and intellectual discourse in Spain. Its influence can be seen in the rise of modern Spanish philosophy and the development of public policy through the active participation of its alumni in governance and society. Furthermore, its extensive library and research facilities support a wide range of scholarly activities, contributing to Spain's position in the global academic community.

As a testament to its significance, the university has been recognized in 55 different language editions of Wikipedia, underscoring its global reach and historical relevance. 'Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world,' as Nelson Mandela stated, encapsulates the ethos of the Complutense University as it continues to educate and inspire future generations.
